statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-116322 (PostgreSQL pre-authentication cancel request can leak a spinlock) affects only PostgreSQL 18. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116322/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, do not list it. The fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/208ea05a51b8e2116323054aa5110f66803a010d, changes only src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c (plus a typedef list), says it is back-patched through 18, and explains that the bug came with a PostgreSQL 18 change after which a starting backend handles a cancel request itself and can hold a shared-memory spinlock at a point where authentication_timeout or SIGTERM can still make it exit. PostgreSQL 16 has neither that file nor that code path: at REL_16_16 the postmaster itself handles a cancel request in processCancelRequest by searching its own list of backends, without taking a spinlock, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_16_16/src/backend/postmaster/postmaster.c . Alpine's postgresql16 16.16-r0 lists CVE-2026-116322 in its secfixes, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, but upstream's own record places PostgreSQL 16 outside the affected range, and none of the Alpine patches applied in that APKBUILD touch cancel handling. This owner covers the packages built from Alpine's postgresql16 recipe: postgresql16 and its subpackages postgresql16-client, -contrib, -contrib-jit, -dev, -doc, -jit, -openrc, -plperl, -plperl-contrib, -plpython3, -plpython3-contrib and -pltcl. We checked every package built from that source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 4 builds (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, each against its index checksum; 16.14-r0 for x86_64 is published without the -plperl-contrib, -plpython3, -plpython3-contrib and -pltcl subpackages. The server binary /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in each build reports its release on both architectures: PostgreSQL 16.13 in 16.13-r0, PostgreSQL 16.14 in 16.14-r0, PostgreSQL 16.15 in 16.15-r0 and PostgreSQL 16.16 in 16.16-r0. Every build is a PostgreSQL 16 release, so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-116322 (PostgreSQL pre-authentication cancel request can leak a spinlock) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116322/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116322, lists only major version 18 as affected. The flaw is that, since PostgreSQL 18, a backend handling a cancel request before authentication compares cancel keys while holding a spinlock in shared memory, so an authentication_timeout or SIGTERM arriving at that moment exits with the lock held. That behaviour came from commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/9d9b9d46f3c509c722ebbf2a1e7dc6296a6c711d ("Move cancel key generation to after forking the backend", first released in PostgreSQL 18), and the fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/208ea05a51b8e2116323054aa5110f66803a010d, changes src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c and is marked back-patch through 18. Commit 9d9b9d46 is not in any PostgreSQL 17 release. At every PostgreSQL 17 release this owner publishes (REL_17_7 through REL_17_12; for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_17_12/src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c), a cancel request is handled by processCancelRequest, which looks up the target in the postmaster's backend list and signals it without taking any spinlock, and src/backend/storage/ipc/procsignal.c has neither the pss_mutex spinlock nor SendCancelRequest. The postgres server binary in every published DHI postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) reports its 17.x release on both x86_64 and aarch64, and none of the Alpine patches applied in the 17.12-r0 APKBUILD touch connection startup or cancel handling. The 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, do not list this CVE. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116322 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-116322), but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 17 outside the affected range.
